meta.notes: Edges filtered: reference===66 AND type==='bechina'. 28 bechina edges found; 16 eitza edges excluded. 12 raw connected components (1×8-node, 1×6-node, 1×5-node, 1×4-node, 1×3-node, 7×2-node) reduced to 5 packages. The central structural axis of this Torah is the Alef-letter encoding the koach/po'al duality (upper-spirit/lower-spirit, beginning-of-thought/end-of-action, YHVH-yud/Adonai-yud). The large components B(6)+C(5)+D(4)+F(2)+K(2) all describe different facets of this single axis and are merged into Package 1. The truth/olam-haba cluster (A=8) absorbs the isolated pair J(הי/שלום שכר) via shared Emet-domain. Speech-perfection (G+L=4) and vowel-points (E=3) remain as independent packages. Anger/livelihood (H+I=4) is the evil/neutral mirror package.

packages.label: כֹּחַ וּפֹעַל — הָאָלֶ"ף
packages.reason: The dominant conceptual structure of Torah #66 is the Alef-letter as the encoding of the koach-po'al (potential-actualization) duality. This package unifies five originally separate but inseparable components: (B) the koach-pole — יו"ד בָּרֹאשׁ (the first yud = Shem haAtzem = beginning of thought = koach = upper spirit/ruach d'le'ela); (C) the po'al-pole — יו"ד בַּסּוֹף (second yud = Shem Adni = end of action = po'al = lower spirit/ruach d'le'tata); (D) the vav/patach — the vav inside the alef that is a bechina of patach (opening), representing the act by which the two yuds are opened and separated when actualization occurs; (F) the combined כֹּחַ וּפֹעַל node equated with the two hands (yadayim = the instruments of manifestation); and (K) the chituch ha-yadayim equated with the verse 'פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ' (the opening of the hands = the actualization event). All five sub-clusters describe the same essential reality from different angles: the pre-actualization state (two yuds bound together, hands not yet open), the moment of actualization (patach/vav opens them), and the resulting structure (right hand = koach, left hand = po'al). The polarity is good because the entire teaching aims at enabling a person to bring their holy intentions from potential into actual practice — from machshavah to ma'aseh. The evil mirror of this package is the evil actualization: 'when a sinner actualizes his sin, he is completely wicked' (line 33) — but those nodes are not in the dataset as bechina edges.
nodes: הַיּוּ"ד שֶׁל שֵׁם הָעֶצֶם, שֶׁהוּא שֵׁם הֲוָיָה בָּרוּךְ הוּא
יוּ"ד שֶׁל הַכִּנּוּי, שֶׁהוּא שֵׁם אֲדֹנָי, שֶׁהוּא יוּ"ד בַּסּוֹף
וָּאו אוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בֵּין שְׁנֵי הַיּוּדִי"ן שֶׁל שְׁנֵי הַשֵּׁמוֹת הַנַּ"ל, כָּזֶה, יאקדונקי

merge_notes.reason: Components B and C are the two poles of the identical structural axis: the upper yud/koach and the lower yud/po'al. They are the two sub-structures that together constitute the alef-letter. In Torah #66 the Rebbe explicitly states 'שְׁנֵי הָרוּחוֹת...הֵם בְּחִינַת כֹּחַ וּפֹעַל' — the two spirits ARE koach and po'al. They are two bechina-components of the same concept, not cause-and-effect. They are separated in the raw graph only because no single bechina-edge directly links the two yuds (the text frames them as a duality, not equating them to each other). Merging them is required: they are both faces of the alef-structure and must be in the same package.

The vav-inside-the-alef IS a bechina of patach (opening). This component describes the same alef-structure as components B and C — it is the mediating element between the two yuds. Its essential nature is 'the opening act' that takes place within the alef, identical to the act of actualizing koach into po'al. Not a cause-and-effect (the vav does not produce the separation — it IS the separation, the opening, the patach state). Merged into Package 1.

The combined node 'כח ופועל' equated to 'שני הידים ימין ושמאל' describes the integrated, realized state of koach-po'al in the bodily instruments of action. This is the same domain as Package 1 — the hands are the site where the alef-structure becomes manifest in the world. The Rebbe explicitly states in lines 26-27: 'שְׁנֵי הָרוּחוֹת...בְּחִינַת שְׁתֵּי הַיָּדַיִם – יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל'. Merged into Package 1.

Chituch ha-yadayim ('cutting/opening of the hands') is stated to be a bechina of 'Potei'ach et yadecha' (Ps 145:16). In the Torah's argument this is the actualization event — when the hands are cut/opened, koach is released into po'al. The acrostic of 'Potei'ach et yadecha' = cha-ta-kh = gematria of 2×ruach. This is entirely within the alef/koach-po'al domain. Its shared bechina-nature with Package 1 is the act-of-opening that is the essence of actualization. Merged into Package 1.

packages.label: אֱמֶת וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא
packages.label_en: Truth and the World to Come
packages.reason: The second large connected component of Torah #66 centers on אֱמֶת (Truth) as the portal through which the World to Come enters this world. All nodes in this cluster are different manifestations of the same ontological reality: divine truth as the foundation of genuine prayer. אֱמֶת = עוֹלָם הַבָּא = עָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי (the coming world) = אֵל (the divine name El, whose essence is truth — 'לֹא אִישׁ אֵל וִיכַזֵּב') = אֵל הֲוָיָה (the combination of El+YHVH in the world of Yetzirah) = יַעֲקֹב (whose seal is truth — 'תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב') = פָּנִים (the Divine Face/Presence — truth is the face of God: 'מְבַקְּשֵׁי פָנֶיךָ יַעֲקֹב סֶלָה') = דִּבּוּר שֶׁל שַׁבָּת (Shabbat speech, which draws the coming-world dimension into weekday speech) = שַׁבָּת itself (which IS a bechina of the World to Come). The small pair הֵי / שִׁלּוּם שָׂכָר (the letter Hei = payment to the wicked in the World to Come) is merged here because the 'payment' (שִׁלּוּם שָׂכָר) of the wicked is precisely how truth/emet manifests as judgment. The Rebbe says: 'אֵל שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינוֹת אֱמֶת, שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ נַעֲשֶׂה שִׁלּוּם שָׂכָר לָרְשָׁעִים' — El=Emet is the agent of the wicked's payment. Hei=payment is thus in the same essential truth-domain. The package describes the positive dimension: these concepts enable a person to pray in truth, free from dependence on other people.

merge_notes.reason: The letter Hei (in the milui/spelled-out form of Shem Havayah) = a bechina of shilum sakhar (payment of wages to the wicked in the World to Come). The source text (section ג, line 55-56) explains this in direct connection to the El-Emet nexus: 'אֵל שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינוֹת אֱמֶת, שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ נַעֲשֶׂה שִׁלּוּם שָׂכָר לָרְשָׁעִים, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינוֹת הֲוָיָה בְּמִלּוּי הֵהִין'. The Hei/payment pair describes how Emet (El=Emet=Package 2) is the agent that brings about the punishment of the wicked. The shared nature is: divine truth-reality as the ultimate arbiter of cosmic justice. This belongs in the truth/olam-haba package, not as an independent domain.

packages.label: שְׁלֵמוּת הַדִּבּוּר
packages.reason: This package groups all nodes describing the essential nature of perfected, complete speech in the weekday world. הַדִּבּוּר בִּשְׁלֵמוּת IS a bechina of שָׂפָה בְּרוּרָה (clear/pure language — the prophetic phrase from Zephaniah 3:9 describing the messianic state when all peoples will call upon God's name). They are the same concept: full, uncorrupted speech. The isolated pair יְמֵי הַחֹל / יְצִירָה is merged here because weekdays = the world of Yetzirah (Formation), which IS the domain of speech in its incomplete form (as the Rebbe states in line 56: 'יְמֵי הַחֹל הֵם בְּחִינוֹת יְצִירָה'). The goal of drawing Shabbat-speech (Package 2's דִּבּוּר שֶׁל שַׁבָּת) into the weekday-speech context IS the achievement of שְׁלֵמוּת הַדִּבּוּר. This is the speech-domain: it describes the state and site of human speech awaiting perfection, as distinct from Package 2's divine truth-domain. The package's polarity is good because שָׂפָה בְּרוּרָה is the eschatological goal and הַדִּבּוּר בִּשְׁלֵמוּת is its positive achievement.

merge_notes.reason: The weekdays (ימי החול) = a bechina of Yetzirah (the world of Formation). The source text (line 56) frames this in direct connection to the speech-perfection theme: 'יְמֵי הַחֹל הֵם בְּחִינוֹת יְצִירָה, כְּשֶׁאֵין אֶחָד בָּהֶם, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינוֹת שַׁבָּת.' The weekday-Yetzirah pair names the domain within which הַדִּבּוּר בִּשְׁלֵמוּת must be drawn into and achieved. They share the same essential nature: the incomplete-speech-world that needs completing. Merged into Package 3.

packages.label: נְקֻדּוֹת וּרְקִיעִין
packages.reason: This three-node component forms an independent and complete bechina-chain: נְקֻדּוֹת (vowel-points) = רְקִיעִין (firmaments) = מְנִיעוֹת (obstacles/barriers). The Rebbe establishes that the nine vowel-points are bechinat the nine firmaments (reki'im), and the firmaments = obstacles (meni'ot). The logic: a rakiya (firmament) is that which separates and blocks — 'יְהִי רָקִיעַ, וִיהִי מַבְדִּיל' — just as an obstacle blocks the person from the desired thing. The nekudah (vowel-point) is produced by desire (cheshek) which itself is intensified by the obstacle. The chain: nekudah = rakiya = meni'ah. This package describes the mechanism by which longing/desire is encoded structurally into the very vowel-points of speech — the 'sound-color' dimension of each letter that carries the intensity of the person's yearning. The polarity is good because the nekudot are the positive medium of genuine speech and the reki'im/meni'ot, although they appear as obstacles, serve the holy purpose of intensifying desire.

packages.label: חֲרוֹן אַף וְנֶזֶק הַפַּרְנָסָה
packages.label_en: Anger and the Damage to Livelihood
packages.reason: This package groups the two isolated pairs that together describe the negative/destructive domain of Torah #66: the bechina-chain of anger→smoke→eyes→livelihood. Charon af (anger) = the smoke that rises from the nostrils (based on Ps 18:9: 'עָלָה עָשָׁן בְּאַפּוֹ'). This smoke = a bechina of damage to parnasah (livelihood) because the eyes (which represent the expectation of livelihood: 'עֵינֵי כֹל אֵלֶיךָ יְשַׂבֵּרוּ' Ps 145:15) are damaged by smoke (Prov 10:26: 'כֶּעָשָׁן לָעֵינָיִם'). This creates the bechina chain: חֲרוֹן אַף = עָשָׁן = נֶזֶק לָעֵינַיִם = עֵינַיִם = פַּרְנָסָה. These four nodes share the same essential nature: the destructive force of anger that blocks the koach→po'al actualization by damaging livelihood (and without livelihood one cannot be free from dependence on others, and without that freedom one cannot pray in truth, and without truth one cannot actualize). This is the evil mirror of the entire teaching: while Package 1 describes holy actualization, Package 5 describes the anger that blocks it. Anger is characterized as 'evil' here because its bechina-language in the text aligns it with the destructive/blocking dimension. The Rebbe teaches that the sweetening of the anger (hamtakat charon af) transforms the smoke into ruach — it is the transition from Package 5 to Package 1.

merge_notes.reason: Eyes = parnasah (livelihood) via Ps 145:15 ('עֵינֵי כֹל אֵלֶיךָ יְשַׂבֵּרוּ'). In the source text (line 24), the Rebbe explains this in direct sequence with the charon-af/smoke pair: 'הֶעָשָׁן מַזִּיק לָעֵינַיִם...שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת פַּרְנָסָה'. The eyes/parnasah pair is the downstream target of the anger-smoke. Their shared bechina-nature with Component I (charon af/smoke) is the destructive domain of anger. Merged into Package 5.
